title: US citizen charged after GrapheneOS phone wipes during airport search
titleZh: 美国公民在机场搜查期间擦拭 GrapheneOS 手机后被指控
author: eecc
relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Serving tech enthusiasts for over 25 years. TechSpot means tech analysis and advice you can trust. A hot potato: A federal case in Atlanta is raising questions about a privacy-focused mobile operating system, with prosecutors arguing that its features were used to erase evidence. The US Department of Justice is attempting to prosecute Atlanta resident Sam Tunick under a federal statute that makes it a crime to destroy property in an effort to prevent it from being seized. The case centers on Tunick's use of GrapheneOS, an open-source operating system that works on Google Pixel phones and lets users enter a passcode to wipe a device clean.

Experts said the legal approach is unusual and may be the first time the law has been aimed at an operating system. "It's concerning – and sends the message that [GrapheneOS] is criminal by default," said Christophe Boutry, a cybersecurity and surveillance expert. Boutry and Bill Buddington, senior staff technologist at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, both said they had not seen a similar case.

The incident began at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on January 24 of last year. Tunick had just returned from a trip to the Dominican Republic when he was stopped for questioning. According to court testimony, federal agents had already circulated his name and photo internally, saying he was under investigation for "suspected terrorism activities" because of his alleged association with the movement against Cop City.

Tunick was taken to a secondary screening room, where multiple agents questioned him. A motion filed by his defense argues the interrogation focused on child sexual abuse material as a pretext for investigating his connections to the protest movement. The motion also states that Tunick asked four times to speak with a lawyer and was denied each time. According to the same filing, agents did not present a warrant or read him his rights.

Government attorneys and agents pushed back during Monday's hearing. They described the encounter as a routine airport inspection. Larry Findley, a Customs and Border Protection officer, said agents were "looking for anything that's prohibited."

comments.author: schoen
comments.textRawHtml:
I co-wrote a border search guide for EFF some years ago. I was very interested in finding clever technical approaches but I later ended up feeling that I hadn't given enough thought to the overall threat model questions (even though the guide did address them, perhaps even somewhat usefully).

The big picture problem is that the agents performing the searches have an enormous amount of power in terms of potentially seizing devices and potentially denying entry for non-citizens. I think they should not have this power, but the agents and courts probably don't care that I think that.

The end result (not inherently different from what we wrote in the guide) is that you may have to think both about protecting your data by technical means, and about not angering the agents more than you plan to. I was fascinated by techniques for being unable to comply (which is straightforward to achieve if you want!) but probably didn't think enough about how much this might antagonize border agents in many cases.

I definitely don't know a comprehensive big-picture solution.
comments.textZhHtml:
几年前，我与他人共同为 EFF 编写了一份边境搜索指南。我对寻找巧妙的技术方法非常感兴趣，但后来我发现我没有对整体威胁模型问题给予足够的考虑（尽管指南确实解决了这些问题，甚至可能有些有用）。

大局问题是，执行搜索的特工拥有巨大的权力，可能会扣押设备并可能拒绝非公民进入。我认为他们不应该拥有这种权力，但代理人和法院可能并不关心我的想法。

最终结果（与我们在指南中编写的内容没有本质上的不同）是，您可能必须考虑通过技术手段保护您的数据，并且不要比您计划的更激怒代理人。我对无法遵守规定的技术很着迷（如果你愿意的话，这很容易实现！），但可能没有充分考虑到在许多情况下这可能会在多大程度上激怒边境人员。

我绝对不知道一个全面的整体解决方案。

children.author: throwawayffffas
children.textRawHtml:
There are 2 cases routine inspections and targeted investigations.

If it's a routine inspection, being uncooperative will probably lead them to escalate. You generally want to keep things routine and boring. If they want to access your device you have to weigh the costs, just log out of everything before you fly and throw away your device after they have had access to it, it's now compromised.

If you are targeted your compliance is irrelevant and only weakens your position, the thing is at the border you don't get all of the protections you get at say a traffic stop they can search everything you have on you without warrants reasonable suspicion or anything.

I am not a lawyer but if you are a citizen they probably can't deny you entry but can probably detain you for an uncomfortable amount of time, and seize whatever they want. Your best defense is to have a burner phone and no other devices nothing they can seize that would hurt you.

For foreign nationals pretty much the same applies except they can deny you entry and ship you off to alligator Alcatraz, just don't fly to America for a few years.

Remember he is not being prosecuted for not handing over his device but for destroying the data they were trying to seize, if he just let them keep the phone he would be Scott free. I.e.the best technical defense is secure encryption with a key thats long enough and not stored on the device.

Actually for the particular case the best technical defense is to not have any data whatsoever on you.
children.textZhHtml:
有2例例行检查和针对性排查。

如果是例行检查，不配合很可能会导致事态升级。你通常想让事情保持常规和无聊。如果他们想要访问您的设备，您必须权衡成本，只需在飞行前注销所有内容，并在他们访问后扔掉您的设备，它现在已受到威胁。

如果您成为目标，您的合规性无关紧要，只会削弱您的地位，问题是在边境，您无法获得所有保护，例如在交通站点，他们可以搜查您身上的所有内容，而无需合理怀疑或其他任何理由。

我不是律师，但如果你是公民，他们可能无法拒绝你入境，但可能会拘留你一段不舒服的时间，并扣押他们想要的任何东西。你最好的防御就是拥有一部一次性手机，不要有其他任何他们可以夺取的设备来伤害你。

对于外国人来说几乎同样适用，除​​了他们可以拒绝你入境并将你送到鳄鱼恶魔岛，只是几年内不要飞往美国。

记住，他不会因为没有交出他的设备而被起诉，而是因为销毁了他们试图夺取的数据，如果他让他们保留手机，他将成为斯科特的自由。也就是说，最好的技术防御是使用足够长且不存储在设备上的密钥进行安全加密。

实际上，对于特定情况，最好的技术防御是不要拥有任何数据。

children.author: tmp10423288442
children.textRawHtml:
> I am not a lawyer but if you are a citizen they probably can't deny you entry but can probably detain you for an uncomfortable amount of time, and seize whatever they want. Your best defense is to have a burner phone and no other devices nothing they can seize that would hurt you.

Even having a burner phone without any personal information on it can be deemed suspicious. It would be best for your phone to have a recently-reinstalled OS, with a few critical apps like Whatsapp or iMessage set up with a few personal messages sent. You need to be able to set those up without a password manager. Anything else needs to take place on devices that you aren't carrying with you. Fortunately enough people don't update their Facebook these days that just having an account that exists but you don't use will probably work, assuming you don't look like someone that would be obsessed with their socials.

Maybe there are USB thumb drives that operate like a YubiKey unless special setup is performed to access the storage inside? That's one way to carry data with you if you have to.
children.textZhHtml:
> 我不是律师，但如果您是公民，他们可能无法拒绝您入境，但可能会拘留您一段不舒服的时间，并扣押他们想要的任何东西。您最好的防御措施是拥有一部一次性手机，并且没有任何其他设备可以抓住，从而对您造成伤害。

即使拥有一部没有任何个人信息的一次性手机也可能被视为可疑。您的手机最好有一个最近重新安装的操作系统，并设置一些重要的应用程序，例如 Whatsapp 或 iMessage，并发送一些个人消息。您需要能够在没有密码管理器的情况下进行设置。其他任何事情都需要在您未随身携带的设备上进行。幸运的是，现在人们不再更新他们的 Facebook，只要拥有一个存在但你不使用的帐户就可能会起作用，假设你看起来不像一个沉迷于社交的人。

也许有 USB 拇指驱动器，其操作方式类似于 YubiKey，除非执行特殊设置来访问内部存储？如果有必要的话，这是随身携带数据的一种方式。

children.author: throwawayffffas
children.textRawHtml:
You can offer the I don't travel with my real phone because it got stolen a bunch of times excuse.

The point is even if they become suspicious all they can do is seize the burner ask you a bunch of questions etc. search you, etc they can't get access to your data. You can't get in real trouble, just majorly inconvenienced.
children.textZhHtml:
你可以提供“我不带着我的真实手机旅行，因为它被偷了很多次”的借口。

重点是，即使他们变得可疑，他们所能做的就是抓住燃烧器问你一堆问题等等。搜查你，等等，他们无法访问你的数据。您不会遇到真正的麻烦，只是带来很大的不便。

children.author: illiac786
children.textRawHtml: If you’re traveling with kids, they have all the leverage they need.
children.textZhHtml: 如果您与孩子一起旅行，他们拥有所需的一切优势。

children.author: mothballed
children.textRawHtml:
You "can't get in real trouble" but teh last time I crossed with basically nothing, they wrote a search warrant by literally fabricating almost everything in it. They wrote that an anonymous dog told an unnamed officer I had drugs, then a completely separate HSI officer signed it and a judge signed it based on complete inter-species hearsay two links removed from any named entity to face to question it.

So yeah you can be imprisoned, brought to ERs while they run up private medical bills (they told doctors I had drugs up my ass), have a search warrant executed, and then at the end of the day be chased by debt collectors for the search that turned up nothing.
children.textZhHtml: 你“不会遇到真正的麻烦”，但上次我基本上什么都没有穿越，他们通过字面意义上捏造了其中的几乎所有内容来写了一份搜查令。 他们写道，一只匿名狗告诉一名未透露姓名的官员我吸毒，然后一名完全独立的 HSI 官员签署了该协议，一名法官根据完整的跨物种传闻签署了该协议，从任何指定实体中删除了两个链接以面对面质疑。什么也没出现。

children.author: amanaplanacanal
children.textRawHtml: How did you get charged money for that? When I go to the hospital, they make me sign a form saying I will be responsible for payment.
children.textZhHtml: 您是如何被收取费用的？当我去医院时，他们让我签署一份表格，说我将负责付款。

children.author: mothballed
children.textRawHtml: I refused to sign anything, they billed it to DHS, DHS refused it and put that I was the responsible party, then the hospital sold it to debt collectors under my name.
children.textZhHtml: 我拒绝签署任何东西，他们向国土安全部开具账单，国土安全部拒绝了，并说我是责任方，然后医院以我的名义将其卖给了收债人。

children.author: cortesoft
children.textRawHtml:
> just log out of everything before you fly and throw away your device after they have had access to it, it's now compromised.

I get what you are saying, but this is incredibly expensive and not really practical for most people.
children.textZhHtml:
> 只需在飞行前注销所有内容即可在他们访问你的设备后扔掉它，它现在已经受到威胁。

我明白你的意思，但这非常昂贵，而且对大多数人来说并不实用。

children.author: fn-mote
children.textRawHtml:
> not really practical for most people

Evaluate your threat model and the chance that a wipe and reinstall of the OS will be insufficient protection.

If you were targeted, you may have some tough choices. Might as well think about them ahead of time.
children.textZhHtml:
> 对于大多数人来说不太实用

评估您的威胁模型以及擦除并重新安装操作系统不足以提供足够保护的可能性。

如果您成为目标，您可能会面临一些艰难的选择。不妨提前考虑一下。

children.author: lentil_soup
children.textRawHtml:
> you may have to think both about protecting your data by technical means, and about not angering the agents more than you plan to

That's the same problem with technical solutions to crime.

I come from a very dangerous city and I used to have a car that needed a PIN to work. You could turn then engine on and drive but after a minute if you didn't input the PIN it would turn off without warning and start blasting the alarm. The idea being that if the car was stolen the thief would be stranded not far from home unsure about what's happening. Great technical solution but it ignores that a lot of the time the car is stolen with you in it (in a kidnapping, for example). Having the car shutoff in the middle of a highway next to a panicking guy with a gun and trying to remember a PIN is not a situation you want to be in, so I just had the PIN number written down on the dashboard, which worked very well when I was eventually kidnapped and just pointed at the piece of paper with the number.
children.textZhHtml:
> 您可能必须考虑通过技术手段保护您的数据，并且不要超出您计划地激怒特工

这对于犯罪的技术解决方案来说也是同样的问题。

我来自一个非常危险的城市，我曾经有一辆需要 PIN 码才能工作的汽车。然后你可以打开引擎并驾驶，但一分钟后，如果你没有输入 PIN 码，它就会在没有警告的情况下关闭并开始发出警报。这个想法是，如果汽车被盗，小偷就会被困在离家不远的地方，不确定发生了什么。很棒的技术解决方案，但它忽略了很多时候汽车在你开着的情况下被盗（例如，在绑架中）。在高速公路中间，汽车被关闭，旁边是一个持枪的惊慌失措的人，并试图记住 PIN 码，这不是你想要的情况，所以我只是将 PIN 码写在仪表板上，当我最终被绑架时，只需指着一张带有数字的纸，这非常有效。

children.author: imglorp
children.textRawHtml:
In phone terms, that's the $5 wrench problem. The elaborate tech is not relevant if you can be simply coerced somehow to bypass it.

Again in phone terms, maybe bring a blank phone through that border.
children.textZhHtml:
用手机术语来说，这就是 5 美元扳手的问题。如果您可以简单地以某种方式强制绕过它，那么复杂的技术就没有意义。

再次用手机术语来说，也许可以带一部空白手机穿过该边界。

children.author: leonidasrup
children.textRawHtml:
Coercion was the reason from start, it's explained in the article.

"A motion filed by his defense argues the interrogation focused on child sexual abuse material as a pretext for investigating his connections to the protest movement."

So the message was simple: don't protest and you will be not harassed.
children.textZhHtml:
胁迫从一开始就是原因，文章中对此进行了解释。

“他的辩护人提出的一项动议认为，审讯的重点是儿童性虐待材料，以此作为调查他与抗议运动的关系的借口。”

因此，信息很简单：不要抗议，你就不会受到骚扰。

children.author: deltoidmaximus
children.textRawHtml: And there's the problem that if the PIN or worse a biometric version of this becomes remotely well known you've now created an incentive for a car thief to kidnap people even if they only want the car.
children.textZhHtml: 问题在于，如果 PIN 或更糟糕的是，其生物识别版本变得众所周知，那么您现在就会激励偷车贼绑架人们，即使他们只是想要汽车。

children.author: TeMPOraL
children.textRawHtml:
Or anything else you can't easily transfer. I can't help but point at passkeys in particular (or 2FA in general).

A variant of this is the well-known scene from a previous century's movie involving extracting an eye to bypass retinal scanner.
children.textZhHtml:
或其他您无法轻松转移的内容。我忍不住要特别指出万能钥匙（或一般的 2FA）。

这种情况的一个变体是上个世纪电影中的著名场景，其中涉及提取眼睛以绕过视网膜扫描仪。

children.author: nilamo
children.textRawHtml: Like when fingerprint readers were added to car doors in the 90s, and carjackers started cutting fingers off to get away...
children.textZhHtml: 就像 90 年代在车门上安装了指纹识别器一样，劫车者开始割断手指以逃脱......

children.author: pinkyboy
children.textRawHtml:
That is a largely incorrect statement that is loosely based on a single incident, not a trend.

The single incident was an individual in Malaysia who added an after-market finger-print based engine immobilizer to his car in 2005. The attackers threatened the individual with machetes, so that he would put his finger on the sensor, and then drove off with him in the car. The attackers later cut off his finger believing it would let them restart it without him present.
children.textZhHtml:
这是一个很大程度上不正确的陈述，它大致基于单一事件，而不是趋势。

该单一事件是马来西亚的一名个人，他于 2005 年在他的汽车上安装了售后指纹式发动机防盗装置。袭击者用砍刀威胁该人，以便他将手指放在传感器上，然后带着他开车离开。 袭击者后来砍掉了他的手指，相信这样他们就可以在他不在场的情况下重新启动手指。

children.author: mapt
children.textRawHtml: As one does.  Why, six of the eleven times I've had my car stolen, it was a carjacking with myself or my family member in it.
children.textZhHtml: 正如人们所做的那样。  为什么，我的车十一次被盗，其中有六次是劫车，车里有我自己或我的家人。

children.author: ryan_j_naughton
children.textRawHtml:
Six of the eleven times...

Crazy.

What city was this, if you don't mind me asking?
children.textZhHtml:
十一次中的六次...

疯狂。

如果你不介意我问的话，这是哪个城市？
